Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · School & learning

correct adjective

right, without mistakes

also right, correctly, accurate, faultless, proper (correct), the proper way, exact, precise, you’re right, you're right, that’s right, speak correctly, spell correctly

classical

Cic. Ac. 1.19: quid vērum, quid falsum, quid rēctum in ōrātiōne prāvumve
Traupman 28, 246
Traupman 297

rēctus, rēcta, rēctum

Declension on Wiktionary

right, correct

The opposite is prāvus (Traupman 28). Latin often uses the adverb: rēctē respondistī, that’s the right answer; rēctē scrībere, to spell correctly (Traupman 29). Of a statement, true: see true.

Other words

  • ēmendātus, ēmendāta, ēmendātum — faultless, free from mistakes

    also used · classical · Quint. 1.5.1: ut ēmendāta, ut dīlūcida, ut ōrnāta sit; Traupman 28, 246, 152; Traupman 297; Traupman 313 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Of speech, writing or reading: corrected, and so without a mistake; the adverb is ēmendātē (Traupman 29).

  • rēctē — correctly, rightly

    adverb · also used · classical · Traupman 29: rēctē loquī (scrībere), to speak (spell) correctly; Traupman 297 · Wiktionary

    The opposite is prāvē.

  • ēmendātē — faultlessly, without mistakes

    adverb · also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. ēmendō; Traupman 29; Traupman 297 · Wiktionary

  • accūrātus, accūrāta, accūrātum — exact, accurate, carefully done

    also used · classical · Traupman 311 · Declension on Wiktionary

  • exāctus, exācta, exāctum — exact, precise

    also used · classical · Traupman 311 · Declension on Wiktionary

Examples

  • certa sit ergō in prīmīs lēctiō, deinde conjūncta et diū lentior, dōnec exercitātiōne contingat ēmendāta vēlōcitās

    let reading first be sure, then joined up, and for a long time rather slow, until practice brings speed without mistakesQuint. 1.1.33

  • Rēctēne scrīpsī? — Rēctē.

    Did I spell it right? — Yes, you did.composed

  • Rēctē dīcis.

    You’re right.Traupman 43

See also true, that’s right, you’re right, mistake, correct, proper, appropriate.
